name: Platycerus quercus
intro: I photographed an adult oak stag beetle in the field.

sections.title: Adults
sections.text: Adults shelter beneath loose bark and in crevices of decaying logs. They have also been collected on blackberry flowers. In Maryland, Staines and Staines collected two adults in a funnel trap between April 5 and 13.

sections.title: Larvae
sections.text: Larvae have been reported from decaying oak logs and stumps. For a trial I would keep an intact section of occupied oak in contact with loose, decayed wood.

sources.title: Staines and Staines, Maryland records of Platycerus quercus
W. Saunders, oak logs and stumps as larval habitat

account_credit: Breeding notes by Junkai Wang and Alan Jeon
